chapters.title: Tobit in Nineveh
chapters.html:
Tobit 1

Tobit and His Tribe

1The book of the words of Tobit son of Tobiel, son of Ananiel, son of Aduel, son of Gabael, of the descendants of Asiel, of the tribe of Naphtali,

2who was taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians from Thisbe, which is south of Kedesh of Naphtali in Galilee, above Asher.

3I, Tobit, walked in the ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life, and I did many acts of charity for my brothers and my nation who had gone with me into captivity to the land of the Assyrians, to Nineveh.

4When I was in my own country, in the land of Israel, while I was still young, the whole tribe of Naphtali my father fell away from the house of Jerusalem, which had been chosen out of all the tribes of Israel for all the tribes to sacrifice there. There the temple, the dwelling of the Most High, was consecrated and built for all generations forever.

5All the tribes that fell away together sacrificed to Baal the heifer, and so did the house of Naphtali my father.

6I alone went often to Jerusalem for the festivals, as it is written for all Israel by an everlasting decree, taking the firstfruits and the tithes of the crops and the first shearings,

7and I gave them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, for the altar. The tenth of all my produce I gave to the sons of Levi who served at Jerusalem. The second tenth I sold, and I went and spent the money in Jerusalem each year.

8The third I gave to those to whom it was due, as Deborah my father's mother had commanded me, for I had been left an orphan by my father.

9When I became a man, I married Anna, a woman of our own family, and by her I had a son, Tobias.

In Nineveh

10When we were carried away captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and those of my race ate the food of the nations,

11but I kept myself from eating it,

12because I remembered God with all my soul.

13The Most High gave me favor and good standing before Shalmaneser, and I became his buyer of supplies.

14I used to go into Media, and once at Rages in Media I left ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael, the brother of Gabrias.

15When Shalmaneser died, Sennacherib his son reigned in his place. His roads became unsafe, and I could no longer go into Media.

16In the days of Shalmaneser I did many acts of charity for my brothers.

17I gave my bread to the hungry and clothing to the naked, and if I saw any of my people dead and thrown out behind the wall of Nineveh, I buried him.

18If King Sennacherib killed any who came fleeing from Judea, I buried them in secret, for in his anger he killed many. When the king looked for the bodies, they could not be found.

19Then one of the men of Nineveh went and informed the king about me, that I was burying them, and I hid. When I learned that I was being sought to be put to death, I was afraid and ran away.

20All my property was seized, and nothing was left to me except Anna my wife and Tobias my son.

21But not fifty days passed before his two sons killed him and fled to the mountains of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place, and he put Ahikar son of Anael, my brother's son, over all the accounts of his kingdom and over all its administration.

22Ahikar spoke for me, and I came back to Nineveh. Ahikar had been cupbearer, keeper of the signet, administrator and treasurer, and Esarhaddon appointed him second to himself. He was my nephew.

Notes

  • v1 "The book of the words of Tobit" — rendered from the Greek, the shorter of its two forms (Swete's main text); the longer Greek is cited where it differs in substance. The names follow the English forms readers know: Greek Enemessar is Shalmaneser (2 Kings 17:3), Sacherdonos is Esarhaddon, and Achiacharus is Ahikar.

  • v3 "acts of charity" — eleēmosynai, from eleos, mercy: mercy shown in what is given. It is the book's word, said of Tobit at the start and taught to his son at the end.

  • v5 "sacrificed to Baal the heifer" — the Greek puts the feminine article before Baal. The longer Greek says plainly to the calf that Jeroboam king of Israel made in Dan (1 Kings 12:28–30).

  • vv6–8 "the firstfruits and the tithes… the second tenth… the third" — three tithes: the Levites' tenth (Numbers 18:21); a second, turned into money and spent in Jerusalem (Deuteronomy 14:22–26); and a third for the guest, the orphan and the widow (14:28–29). Tobit, an orphan himself, gives the third.

  • vv10–12 "I kept myself from eating it" — as Daniel would in Babylon: Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's food (Daniel 1:8).

  • vv15, 18 "Sennacherib" — the Greek held here reads Acherel, a name found nowhere else. The longer Greek has Sennacherim, and v21 tells his end as Kings tells Sennacherib's: his two sons killed him and fled to the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place (2 Kings 19:37).

  • vv17–18 "I buried him" — the act the whole story turns on: Tobit's burying of the dead costs him his goods here and his sight in the next chapter.

  • vv21–22 "Ahikar… my nephew" — the highest official of the Assyrian court is family, and the reason Tobit can come home.

chapters.title: Tobit Blinded
chapters.html:
Tobit 2

The Feast of Weeks

1When I had come home and Anna my wife and Tobias my son had been given back to me, at the festival of Pentecost, which is the holy festival of seven weeks, a good dinner was prepared for me, and I reclined to eat.

2I saw the many dishes, and I said to my son, "Go and bring whatever poor man you find among our brothers who remembers the Lord. I will wait for you."

3He came back and said, "Father, one of our people has been strangled and thrown out in the marketplace."

4Before I had tasted anything, I sprang up and carried him into a room until the sun went down.

5Then I came back, washed myself and ate my bread in sorrow.

6I remembered the prophecy of Amos, how he said, "Your festivals shall be turned into mourning, and all your merrymaking into lamentation."

7I wept. When the sun had gone down, I went and dug a grave and buried him.

8My neighbors laughed at me and said, "He is no longer afraid of being put to death for this. He ran away, and here he is burying the dead again."

The Sparrows

9That same night, after I had buried him, I came back, and because I was unclean I slept by the wall of the courtyard, with my face uncovered.

10I did not know that there were sparrows in the wall. My eyes were open, and the sparrows dropped warm droppings into my eyes, and white films formed on my eyes. I went to physicians, but they did not help me. Ahikar took care of me until he went to Elymais.

Anna and the Goat

11My wife Anna earned money at women's work,

12and she sent it to the owners, and they paid her wages and also gave her a young goat.

13When she came back to me, the goat began to bleat. I said to her, "Where did this kid come from? It was not stolen, was it? Give it back to its owners, for it is not right to eat anything stolen."

14She said, "It was given to me as a gift, besides my wages." But I did not believe her, and I told her to give it back to its owners, and I flushed with anger at her. Then she answered me, "Where are your acts of charity and your righteous deeds? See, everything about you is plain to see."

Notes

  • v1 "the festival of Pentecost, which is the holy festival of seven weeks" — Pentecost, the fiftieth, the Greek name for the Festival of Weeks, kept seven weeks after the harvest began (Deuteronomy 16:9–10).

  • v2 "whatever poor man you find… who remembers the Lord" — Tobit's charity at his own table: the feast is for a guest who is poor and faithful.

  • v6 "Your festivals shall be turned into mourning" — Amos 8:10, I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation. Tobit's feast is turned exactly so.

  • v9 "because I was unclean" — whoever touches a dead body is unclean seven days (Numbers 19:11), so he does not go into the house.

  • v10 "white films formed on my eyes" — leukōmata, white spots, a clouding of the eye. The longer Greek says the droppings brought on the white films. Tobit's blindness comes from his burying of the dead, and the physicians cannot help.

  • v14 "Where are your acts of charity and your righteous deeds?" — Anna turns his own words against him (1:3). The reproach of a wife to a righteous man struck down recalls Job's: Do you still hold fast your integrity? (Job 2:9).

chapters.title: Two Prayers on One Day
chapters.html:
Tobit 3

Tobit's Prayer

1Then in my grief I wept, and in my anguish I prayed, saying,

2"You are righteous, O Lord, and all Your works and all Your ways are mercy and truth, and You judge with true and righteous judgment forever.

3Remember me and look on me. Do not punish me for my sins and for my unknowing errors, and those of my fathers, which they sinned before You.

4For they disobeyed Your commandments, and You gave us over to plunder, to captivity and to death, a byword of reproach among all the nations among whom we have been scattered.

5Now Your many judgments are true in dealing with me for my sins and those of my fathers, because we did not keep Your commandments, for we did not walk in truth before You.

6So now deal with me as it pleases You. Command my spirit to be taken from me, so that I may be released and become earth. It is better for me to die than to live, because I have heard false reproaches, and there is great sorrow in me. Command that I be released from this distress now to the everlasting place. Do not turn Your face away from me."

Sarah in Ecbatana

7On that same day it happened to Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, in Ecbatana of Media, that she also was reproached by her father's maids,

8because she had been given to seven husbands, and Asmodeus the evil demon had killed each of them before they had been with her as with a wife. The maids said to her, "Do you not know that you strangle your husbands? You have already had seven, and you have not had the benefit of one of them.

9Why do you beat us? If they are dead, go with them! May we never see a son or daughter of yours!"

10When she heard these things, she was so grieved that she thought of hanging herself. But she said, "I am my father's only child. If I do this, it will be a disgrace to him, and I will bring his old age down in sorrow to Hades."

Sarah's Prayer

11So she prayed by the window and said, "Blessed are You, O Lord my God, and blessed is Your holy and honored name forever. May all Your works bless You forever.

12And now, O Lord, I have set my eyes and my face toward You.

13Command that I be released from the earth, so that I may no longer hear reproach.

14You know, O Lord, that I am innocent of any sin with a man,

15and that I have not defiled my name or the name of my father in the land of my captivity. I am my father's only child, and he has no child to be his heir, and no near kinsman or son of his to whom I should keep myself as a wife. Already seven husbands of mine have died. Why should I live? But if it does not please You to kill me, command that You look on me and have mercy on me, and that I no longer hear reproach."

Raphael Sent

16The prayer of both was heard before the glory of the great God,

17and Raphael was sent to heal the two of them: to scale away the white films from Tobit's eyes, and to give Sarah the daughter of Raguel as a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit, and to bind Asmodeus the evil demon, because Tobias had the right to inherit her. At that very time Tobit came back and went into his house, and Sarah the daughter of Raguel came down from her upper room.

Notes

  • v2 "all Your ways are mercy and truth" — eleēmosynai, the word of Tobit's own acts of charity (1:3; 2:14). What he gave to his brothers, he names in God.

  • v6 "It is better for me to die than to live" — the prayer of Elijah under the broom tree, Now, LORD, take my life (1 Kings 19:4), and of Jonah, it is better for me to die than to live (Jonah 4:3).

  • v7 "On that same day" — two people in two cities, Nineveh and Ecbatana, pray to die on the same day, and the two stories become one.

  • v10 "I will bring his old age down in sorrow to Hades" — Jacob's words when he would not let Benjamin go: you will bring my gray head down in sorrow to Sheol (Genesis 42:38). Hades is the Greek for Sheol, and Tobit has the words of the Greek Genesis.

  • v11 "she prayed by the window" — as Daniel prayed in his upper room, with its windows open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:10).

  • vv16–17 "before the glory of the great God, and Raphael was sent" — the Greek held here reads before the glory of the great Raphael, and was sent; the longer Greek has before the glory of God. The rendering follows the longer Greek for God. Raphael is a Hebrew name, God heals, and he is sent to heal the two.

  • v17 "because Tobias had the right to inherit her" — as the nearest kinsman. The law kept a daughter who inherits within her father's tribe (Numbers 36:8).

chapters.title: Tobit's Charge to His Son
chapters.html:
Tobit 4

"Remember the Lord"

1On that day Tobit remembered the money that he had left in trust with Gabael at Rages in Media,

2and he said to himself, "I have asked for death. Why do I not call my son Tobias and tell him about it before I die?"

3So he called him and said, "My child, when I die, bury me, and do not neglect your mother. Honor her all the days of your life. Do what pleases her, and do not grieve her.

4Remember, my child, that she faced many dangers for you while you were in her womb. When she dies, bury her beside me in one grave.

5My child, remember the Lord our God all your days, and do not set your will to sin or to break His commandments. Do what is right all the days of your life, and do not walk in the ways of wrongdoing.

6For if you act in truth, you will prosper in all your works, as do all who do what is right.

Charity

7Give charity from what you have, and do not let your eye begrudge it when you give. Do not turn your face away from any poor man, and the face of God will not be turned away from you.

8If you have much, give from it in proportion. If you have little, do not be afraid to give according to the little you have.

9So you will be storing up a good treasure for yourself against the day of need.

10For charity delivers from death and keeps one from going into the darkness.

11Charity is a good offering in the sight of the Most High for all who give it.

Marriage and Conduct

12Beware, my child, of all sexual immorality. Above all take a wife from the descendants of your fathers. Do not take a foreign wife, who is not of your father's tribe, for we are the sons of the prophets. Remember, my child, Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, our fathers of old: they all took wives from among their own kindred, and they were blessed in their children, and their descendants will inherit the land.

13So now, my child, love your brothers, and do not in your heart be too proud toward your brothers and the sons and daughters of your people to take a wife for yourself from among them. For in pride there is ruin and much confusion, and in idleness there is loss and great want, for idleness is the mother of famine.

14Do not keep back overnight the wages of any man who works for you, but pay him at once. If you serve God, you will be repaid. Watch yourself, my child, in all that you do, and be disciplined in all your conduct.

15What you hate, do not do to anyone. Do not drink wine to drunkenness, and do not let drunkenness go with you on your way.

16Give of your bread to the hungry and of your clothing to the naked. Give all your surplus as charity, and do not let your eye begrudge it when you give.

17Pour out your bread on the grave of the righteous, but give none to sinners.

18Seek advice from every wise man, and do not despise any useful counsel.

19At all times bless the Lord God, and ask Him that your ways may be made straight and that all your paths and plans may prosper. For no nation has counsel of its own; the Lord Himself gives all good things, and He humbles whom He wills, as He wills. So now, my child, remember my commands, and do not let them be blotted out of your heart.

The Money in Media

20And now I tell you about the ten talents of silver that I left in trust with Gabael son of Gabrias at Rages in Media.

21Do not be afraid, my child, because we have become poor. You have great wealth if you fear God and turn away from all sin and do what is pleasing in His sight."

Notes

  • vv3–4 "Honor her all the days of your life… bury her beside me in one grave" — the commandment, Honor your father and your mother (Exodus 20:12), given its last duty: a grave shared.

  • vv7–11 "charity" — eleēmosynē, the book's word (1:3), five times in five verses. Charity delivers from death (v10) is the proverb, righteousness delivers from death (Proverbs 10:2), with charity where Proverbs has righteousness.

  • v7 "Do not turn your face away from any poor man, and the face of God will not be turned away from you" — a measure for measure: the face turned to the poor is answered by God's face.

  • v12 "for we are the sons of the prophets… Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob" — the fathers are called prophets, and marriage within the family is set beside the blessing of their children. Sarah, the bride the story is preparing, is of Tobit's own kindred (3:17).

  • v14 "Do not keep back overnight the wages" — the law: The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight until morning (Leviticus 19:13).

  • v15 "What you hate, do not do to anyone" — the rule in its negative form. Jesus gives it in its positive form: whatever you want people to do to you, do the same to them (Matthew 7:12).

  • v16 "Give of your bread to the hungry and of your clothing to the naked" — Isaiah's fast: to share your bread with the hungry… when you see the naked, to cover him (Isaiah 58:7). It is what Tobit did (1:17).

  • v17 "Pour out your bread on the grave of the righteous" — the sense is uncertain: perhaps food given to the family of a righteous man who has died, at the meal of mourning.

chapters.title: A Companion for the Journey
chapters.html:
Tobit 5

Tobias Finds a Guide

1Tobias answered him, "Father, I will do everything you have commanded me.

2But how can I get the money, when I do not know him?"

3So he gave him the signed receipt and said to him, "Find yourself a man to go with you, and I will pay him wages while I live. Go and get the money."

5He said to him, "Can I go with you to Rages in Media? Do you know the region?"

6The angel said to him, "I will go with you. I know the way, and I have lodged with Gabael our brother."

7Tobias said to him, "Wait for me, and I will tell my father."

8He said to him, "Go, and do not be long."

9He went in and said to his father, "I have found someone who will go with me." He said, "Call him to me, so that I may learn what tribe he is from and whether he can be trusted to go with you."

10So he called him, and he came in, and they greeted each other.

11Tobit said to him, "Brother, what tribe and what family are you from? Tell me."

12He said to him, "Are you looking for a tribe and a family, or for a hired man to go with your son?" Tobit said to him, "Brother, I want to know your family and your name."

13He said, "I am Azarias, son of Ananias the great, one of your brothers."

14Tobit said to him, "Welcome, brother. Do not be angry with me because I wanted to know your tribe and your family. You are my brother, of a good and noble line. I knew Ananias and Jathan, the sons of Shemaiah the great, when we went together to Jerusalem to worship, bringing the firstborn and the tithes of the crops, and they did not go astray when our brothers went astray. You come of good stock, brother.

15But tell me, what wages shall I pay you? A drachma a day, and your expenses, as for my son?

16I will add something to your wages if you both come back safe and sound."

17So they agreed. Then he said to Tobias, "Get ready for the journey, and may you have a good journey." His son prepared what he needed for the journey, and his father said to him, "Go with this man. Anna's Tears

18But Anna his mother wept and said to Tobit, "Why have you sent our child away? Is he not the staff of our hand as he goes in and out before us?

19Do not add money to money. Let it be as refuse compared with our child.

20For the life the Lord has given us to live is enough for us."

21Tobit said to her, "Do not worry, my sister. He will come back safe and sound, and your eyes will see him.

  • v17 "may His angel go with you… and the young man's dog went with them" — Tobit prays for an angel to go with his son, not knowing one stands in front of him. The dog goes too, and is with Tobias again on the way home (11:4).

  • v22 "a good angel will go with him" — Tobit says it to comfort his wife; it is literally true.

chapters.title: The Fish in the Tigris
chapters.html:
Tobit 6

The Fish

1So she stopped weeping.

2As they went on their way, they came in the evening to the Tigris River, and they camped there.

3The young man went down to wash himself, and a fish leaped up out of the river and tried to swallow the young man.

4The angel said to him, "Take hold of the fish." The young man seized the fish and threw it up on the land.

5The angel said to him, "Cut the fish open, and take the heart, the liver and the gall, and keep them safe."

6The young man did as the angel told him. They roasted the fish and ate it, and the two of them went on until they came near Ecbatana.

7The young man said to the angel, "Brother Azarias, what are the liver, the heart and the gall of the fish for?"

8He said to him, "As for the heart and the liver, if a demon or an evil spirit troubles anyone, you burn them before the man or woman, and the person will never be troubled again.

9As for the gall, anoint a man who has white films on his eyes, and he will be healed."

Sarah Promised

10When they drew near to Ecbatana,

11the angel said to the young man, "Brother, today we will stay with Raguel. He is your relative, and he has a daughter named Sarah.

12I will speak about her, that she be given to you as your wife, for her inheritance falls to you, and you alone are of her family. The girl is beautiful and sensible.

13So now listen to me, and I will speak to her father, and when we come back from Rages we will celebrate the marriage. For I know that Raguel cannot give her to another man according to the law of Moses without incurring death, because the right to the inheritance falls to you rather than to any other man."

14Then the young man said to the angel, "Brother Azarias, I have heard that the girl has been given to seven husbands and that they all died in the bridal chamber.

15Now I am my father's only son, and I am afraid that if I go in to her I will die as those before me did, for a demon loves her, and it harms no one except those who come near her. So now I am afraid that I will die and bring my father's and my mother's life down to their grave in sorrow over me. They have no other son to bury them."

16The angel said to him, "Do you not remember the words your father commanded you, that you should take a wife from your own family? So now listen to me, brother, for she will be your wife. Do not give the demon another thought, for this very night she will be given to you as your wife.

17When you go into the bridal chamber, take live ashes of incense and put some of the heart and the liver of the fish on them, and make smoke.

18The demon will smell it and flee, and will never come back again. When you go to her, rise up, both of you, and cry out to the merciful God, and He will save you and have mercy on you. Do not be afraid, for she was set apart for you from the beginning. You will save her, and she will go with you, and I suppose you will have children by her." When Tobias heard these things, he loved her, and his soul clung to her greatly.

Notes

  • vv3–4 "a fish leaped up out of the river and tried to swallow the young man" — what threatens to swallow him becomes the means of healing his father and freeing his bride.

  • vv8–9 "the heart and the liver… the gall" — the angel gives the remedies before the reader knows what they will be for: one for Sarah's demon (3:8), one for Tobit's white films (2:10).

  • vv6, 10 "until they came near Ecbatana… When they drew near to Ecbatana" — Raguel lives in Ecbatana (3:7). In v10 the Greek held here reads Rages, where the money is, and the angel speaks of going on to Rages afterward (v13). The longer Greek has Ecbatana, which the rendering follows.

  • v13 "according to the law of Moses" — the law that kept an heiress's inheritance within her father's tribe (Numbers 36:8).

  • v15 "a demon loves her" — the Greek says philei, loves. Sarah's affliction is a jealous demon, and it kills only those who come near her.

  • v18 "she was set apart for you from the beginning… his soul clung to her greatly" — ekollēthē, the verb of Genesis, a man… clings to his woman (Genesis 2:24 in the Greek). Tobias loves her before he has seen her.

chapters.title: At Raguel's House
chapters.html:
Tobit 7

The Welcome

1They came to Ecbatana and arrived at the house of Raguel, and Sarah came to meet them. She greeted them and they greeted her, and she brought them into the house.

2Raguel said to Edna his wife, "How much the young man looks like my cousin Tobit!"

3Raguel asked them, "Where are you from, brothers?" They said to him, "We are of the sons of Naphtali, the captives in Nineveh."

4He said to them, "Do you know our brother Tobit?"

5They said, "He is alive and well." Tobias said, "He is my father."

6Raguel sprang up and kissed him and wept,

7and he blessed him and said to him, "You are the son of a good and noble man!" When he heard that Tobit had lost his sight, he was grieved and wept.

8Edna his wife and Sarah his daughter also wept, and they received them warmly.

The Marriage

9They slaughtered a ram from the flock and set out many dishes. Then Tobias said to Raphael, "Brother Azarias, speak about the things you talked of on the way, and let the matter be settled."

10So he passed the word to Raguel. Raguel said to Tobias, "Eat, drink and be merry, for it is right for you to take my child. But I will show you the truth.

11I have given my child to seven men, and whenever they went in to her, they died in the night. But for now, be merry." Tobias said, "I will taste nothing here until you make an agreement and stand by it with me." Raguel said, "Take her from now on, according to the law. You are her kinsman, and she is yours. The merciful God will give you both the best of success."

12He called his daughter Sarah, took her by the hand and gave her to Tobias as his wife, and said, "Take her according to the law of Moses, and lead her away to your father." Then he blessed them.

13He called Edna his wife, and he took a scroll and wrote out a contract, and they set their seals to it.

14Then they began to eat.

15Raguel called Edna his wife and said to her, "Sister, prepare the other room and take her into it."

16She did as he said and took her there, and Sarah wept. Her mother received her daughter's tears and said to her,

17"Take courage, my child. May the Lord of heaven and earth give you joy in place of this sorrow of yours. Take courage, my daughter."

Notes

  • v2 "How much the young man looks like my cousin Tobit" — anepsios, a cousin or near kinsman. Raguel sees the father in the son's face before he knows whose son he is.

  • v11 "I will taste nothing here until you make an agreement" — as Abraham's servant said in the house of Rebekah's family, I will not eat until I have spoken my words (Genesis 24:33): the marriage is settled before the meal.

  • v11 "You are her kinsman" — adelphos, brother, used of a near relative, as Tobit calls his wife sister (5:21) and Raguel calls Edna sister (v15).

  • v13 "he took a scroll and wrote out a contract" — syngraphē, a written marriage contract, sealed by both parents.

  • v17 "May the Lord of heaven and earth give you joy in place of this sorrow" — charin, grace, joy. A mother sends her daughter into the room where seven husbands died.

chapters.title: The Wedding Night
chapters.html:
Tobit 8

The Demon Driven Out

1When they had finished eating, they brought Tobias in to her.

2As he went, he remembered the words of Raphael, and he took the live ashes of incense and put the heart and the liver of the fish on them, and made smoke.

3When the demon smelled the odor, it fled to the farthest parts of Egypt, and the angel bound it.

The Prayer of Tobias

4When the two of them were shut in together, Tobias got up from the bed and said, "Sister, get up, and let us pray that the Lord may have mercy on us."

5Tobias began to say, "Blessed are You, O God of our fathers, and blessed is Your holy and glorious name forever. Let the heavens and all Your creation bless You.

6You made Adam and gave him Eve his wife as a helper and support. From them the race of mankind has come. You said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone; let us make him a helper like himself.'

7And now, O Lord, I am not taking this sister of mine because of lust, but in truth. Command that I may find mercy and that we may grow old together."

8She said with him, "Amen."

Raguel's Grave

9They both slept through the night. Raguel got up and went and dug a grave,

10saying, "Perhaps this one will die too."

11Then Raguel came into his house,

12and said to Edna his wife, "Send one of the maids to see whether he is alive. If he is not, let us bury him so that no one knows."

13The maid opened the door and went in, and found the two of them asleep.

14She came out and told them that he was alive.

15Raguel blessed God, saying, "Blessed are You, O God, with every blessing. Let Your holy ones and all Your creation bless You. Let all Your angels and Your chosen ones bless You forever.

16Blessed are You, because You have made me glad. It has not happened to me as I feared, but You have dealt with us according to Your great mercy.

17Blessed are You, because You have had mercy on two only children. Show them mercy, O Master, and bring their lives to completion in health, with gladness and mercy."

18Then he ordered his servants to fill in the grave.

The Wedding Feast

19He gave them a wedding feast of fourteen days.

20Before the days of the wedding were over, Raguel made him swear not to leave until the fourteen days of the wedding were complete,

21and then to take half of his property and go back in health to his father; "and the rest," he said, "when my wife and I die."

Notes

  • v3 "it fled to the farthest parts of Egypt, and the angel bound it" — the binding Raphael was sent to do (3:17).

  • v6 "It is not good for the man to be alone; let us make him a helper like himself" — the words of Genesis in its Greek: let us make him a helper corresponding to him (Genesis 2:18). Tobias prays the first marriage over his own.

  • v7 "not because of lust, but in truth" — porneia, the word of Tobit's warning (4:12). The son keeps his father's charge on the night it is tested.

  • vv9–18 "Raguel got up and went and dug a grave" — in a book that began with Tobit burying the dead, the bride's father digs a grave for the groom, and fills it in again at dawn.

  • vv15–17 "Blessed are You… because You have had mercy on two only children" — monogeneis, both of them the only child of their parents (3:15; 6:15).

chapters.title: The Money Brought from Rages
chapters.html:
Tobit 9

Raphael Goes to Gabael

1Tobias called Raphael and said to him,

2"Brother Azarias, take a servant and two camels with you, and go to Gabael at Rages in Media, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.

3For Raguel has sworn that I must not leave,

4and my father is counting the days, and if I am long delayed, he will be very distressed."

5So Raphael went and stayed overnight with Gabael, and gave him the signed receipt. Gabael brought out the bags with their seals intact and gave them to him.

6They set out together early in the morning and came to the wedding, and Tobias blessed his wife.

Notes

  • v2 "bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding" — the errand the whole journey was for is done in four verses, by the angel, while the young man stays at his wedding.

  • v4 "my father is counting the days" — the next chapter opens with Tobit doing just that (10:1).

  • v5 "the bags with their seals intact" — the ten talents left in trust in 1:14, returned untouched after all Tobit's misfortunes.

  • v6 "Tobias blessed his wife" — so the shorter Greek. The longer Greek has Gabael come in, find Tobias at table, and bless him and his wife.

chapters.title: The Parents Wait
chapters.html:
Tobit 10

Tobit and Anna Wait

1Tobit his father was counting each day. When the days for the journey had passed and he did not come,

2he said, "Can he have been put to shame? Or can Gabael have died, and there is no one to give him the money?"

3He was very distressed.

4His wife said to him, "The child has perished, because he is so long in coming." She began to mourn for him and said,

5"Do I not care, my child, that I let you go, you who are the light of my eyes?"

6Tobit said to her, "Be quiet. Do not worry. He is well."

7She said to him, "Be quiet. Do not deceive me. My child has perished." Every day she went out to the road by which he had gone. By day she ate no bread, and through the nights she did not stop mourning for her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the wedding were over that Raguel had sworn to have him spend there. Then Tobias said to Raguel, "Let me go, for my father and my mother no longer hope to see me."

8His father-in-law said to him, "Stay with me, and I will send to your father, and they will tell him how things are with you."

9But Tobias said, "Let me go to my father."

10So Raguel got up and gave him Sarah his wife and half of his property, servants and cattle and money.

11He blessed them and sent them away, saying, "The God of heaven will give you a good journey, my children, before I die."

12He said to his daughter, "Honor your father-in-law and your mother-in-law. They are now your parents. May I hear a good report of you." Then he kissed her. Edna said to Tobias, "Dear brother, may the Lord of heaven bring you back safely, and may He grant me to see your children by my daughter Sarah, so that I may rejoice before the Lord. I am entrusting my daughter to you in trust. Do not grieve her."

Notes

  • v1 "Tobit his father was counting each day" — as Tobias said he would be (9:4). The book moves between the two houses, the wedding in Ecbatana and the waiting in Nineveh.

  • v5 "you who are the light of my eyes" — Anna says it to a son who is not there, in a house where her husband cannot see.

  • v7 "Every day she went out to the road by which he had gone" — she keeps watch there until she sees him coming (11:5–6).

  • v10 "servants and cattle" — sōmata kai ktēnē, bodies and cattle: bodies is the word for slaves.

  • v12 "I am entrusting my daughter to you in trust" — paratithemai… en parakatathēkē, the words used of Tobit's money left in trust with Gabael (1:14; 4:20). The book began with silver given in trust; it ends its journey with a daughter given in trust.

chapters.title: Tobit's Sight Restored
chapters.html:
Tobit 11

The Return

1After this Tobias went on his way, blessing God that He had given him a good journey, and he blessed Raguel and Edna his wife. He went on until he came near Nineveh.

2Raphael said to Tobias, "Brother, do you not know how you left your father?

3Let us run ahead of your wife and prepare the house.

4Take the gall of the fish in your hand." So they went on, and the dog came along behind them.

5Anna sat looking down the road for her son.

6She saw him coming, and she said to his father, "Your son is coming, and the man who went with him!"

7Raphael said, "I know that your father will open his eyes.

8Rub the gall on his eyes. It will sting, and he will rub them and throw off the white films, and he will see you."

9Anna ran to her son and fell on his neck, and said to him, "I have seen you, my child. Now I can die." Then they both wept.

The Healing

10Tobit came out toward the door, stumbling, but his son ran to him

11and took hold of his father, and he sprinkled the gall on his father's eyes, saying, "Take courage, father."

12When they stung, he rubbed his eyes,

13and the white films peeled away from the corners of his eyes. When he saw his son, he fell on his neck,

14and he wept and said, "Blessed are You, O God, and blessed is Your name forever, and blessed are all Your holy angels.

15For You have scourged me, and You have had mercy on me. I see my son Tobias!" His son went in rejoicing and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.

The Bride Welcomed

16Tobit went out to meet his daughter-in-law at the gate of Nineveh, rejoicing and blessing God. Those who saw him walking marveled that he could see.

17Tobit gave thanks before them that God had had mercy on him. When Tobit came near Sarah his daughter-in-law, he blessed her, saying, "Welcome, my daughter. Blessed is God who has brought you to us, and blessed are your father and your mother." There was joy among all his brothers in Nineveh.

18Ahikar and his nephew Nasbas came,

19and Tobias's wedding was celebrated with joy for seven days.

Notes

  • v4 "the dog came along behind them" — the dog that set out with them (5:17) comes home with them.

  • v9 "I have seen you, my child. Now I can die" — the words of Jacob to Joseph in Egypt: Now let me die, since I have seen your face (Genesis 46:30, in the Greek I will die from now on).

  • vv10–13 "stumbling… the white films peeled away" — elepisthē, the verb of 3:17, where Raphael was sent to scale away the films. What was prayed for in chapter 3 happens in the words of chapter 3.

  • v15 "You have scourged me, and You have had mercy on me" — the confession Tobit will put into his song: He scourges and He shows mercy (13:2).

  • v16 "Tobit went out to meet his daughter-in-law… they marveled that he could see" — the Greek held here names Tobias; the longer Greek names no one, and the verse is about the man who now can see. The rendering names Tobit.

  • v18 "Ahikar and his nephew Nasbas" — Tobit's nephew, who cared for him in his blindness (2:10) comes to the wedding.

chapters.title: Raphael Makes Himself Known
chapters.html:
Tobit 12

The Wages

1Tobit called his son Tobias and said to him, "My child, see to the wages of the man who went with you, and you must give him something more."

2He said, "Father, it does me no harm to give him half of what I have brought back,

3for he has brought me back to you safe and sound, he healed my wife, he brought my money, and he healed you as well."

4The old man said, "It is his due."

5So he called the angel and said to him, "Take half of all that you two have brought back."

The Angel's Words

6Then he called the two of them aside privately and said to them, "Bless God and give thanks to Him. Ascribe greatness to Him, and give thanks to Him before all the living for what He has done for you. It is good to bless God and to exalt His name, making known with honor the works of God. Do not be slow to give Him thanks.

7It is good to keep a king's secret, but to reveal the works of God gloriously. Do good, and evil will not find you.

8Prayer is good with fasting, charity and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with wrongdoing. It is better to give charity than to store up gold.

9Charity delivers from death and will purge away every sin. Those who give charity and do righteous deeds will be filled with life,

10but those who sin are enemies of their own lives.

11I will not hide anything from you. I have said, 'It is good to keep a king's secret, but to reveal the works of God gloriously.'

12So now, when you prayed, you and your daughter-in-law Sarah, I brought the record of your prayer before the Holy One, and when you buried the dead, I was with you likewise.

13When you did not hesitate to get up and leave your dinner to go and lay out the dead, your good deed did not escape me; I was with you.

14And now God has sent me to heal you and your daughter-in-law Sarah.

15I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One."

16The two of them were shaken and fell on their faces, for they were afraid.

17He said to them, "Do not be afraid; you will have peace. Bless God forever.

18For I came not by any favor of my own, but by the will of your God. So bless Him forever.

19All these days I appeared to you, but I did not eat or drink; you were seeing a vision.

20Now give thanks to God, for I am going up to Him who sent me. Write in a book everything that has happened."

21They stood up, and they did not see him anymore.

22They gave thanks for His great and wonderful works, and that the angel of the Lord had appeared to them.

Notes

  • vv7, 11 "It is good to keep a king's secret, but to reveal the works of God gloriously" — said twice. Proverbs says the reverse of a king: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings to search out a thing (Proverbs 25:2). The angel has kept his own secret until now, and now reveals the works of God.

  • vv8–9 "Charity delivers from death and will purge away every sin" — Tobit's charge to his son (4:10), now in the angel's mouth, with more: purge away every sin.

  • vv12–13 "I brought the record of your prayer before the Holy One… when you buried the dead, I was with you" — mnēmosynon, a memorial, the word the angel speaks to Cornelius: Your prayers and your alms have gone up as a memorial before God (Acts 10:4). The burial at the Feast of Weeks (2:3–7), which cost Tobit his sight, was seen.

  • v15 "one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the saints" — Revelation sees the seven angels who stand before God, and the incense rising with the prayers of the saints (Revelation 8:2–4).

  • v19 "I did not eat or drink; you were seeing a vision" — the book had them roast the fish and eat it together (6:6). The angel says now that what they saw him do was appearance.

  • v20 "Write in a book everything that has happened" — the book gives its own reason for being written.

chapters.title: Tobit's Song of Praise
chapters.html:
Tobit 13

"He Scourges and Shows Mercy"

1Then Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing and said:
"Blessed is God who lives forever,
and blessed is His kingdom.

2For He scourges and He shows mercy;
He brings down to Hades and brings up again,
and there is no one who can escape His hand.

3Give thanks to Him, sons of Israel, before the nations,
for He has scattered us among them.

4There make known His greatness;
exalt Him before every living thing,
for He is our Lord,
and He is our God and our Father forever.

5He will scourge us for our wrongdoings,
and He will have mercy again,
and will gather us from all the nations
among whom you have been scattered.

6If you turn to Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
to do what is true before Him,
then He will turn to you
and will not hide His face from you.
See what He will do with you,
and give thanks to Him with your whole body.
Bless the Lord of righteousness,
and exalt the King of the ages.
In the land of my captivity I give Him thanks,
and I show His strength and His greatness to a nation of sinners.
Turn back, you sinners, and do what is right before Him.
Who knows whether He will accept you and show you mercy?

7I exalt my God,
and my soul exalts the King of heaven,
and will rejoice in His greatness.

8Let all speak,
and give thanks to Him in Jerusalem.

Jerusalem

9Jerusalem, holy city,
He will scourge you for the deeds of your sons,
but He will again have mercy on the sons of the righteous.

10Give thanks to the Lord worthily,
and bless the King of the ages,
so that His tent may be built in you again with joy.
May He make glad in you those who are captives,
and love in you those who are in distress,
for all generations forever.

11Many nations will come from far away to the name of the Lord God,
bearing gifts in their hands, gifts for the King of heaven.
Generations of generations will give you rejoicing.

12Cursed are all who hate you;
blessed forever will be all who love you.

13Rejoice and be glad over the sons of the righteous,
for they will be gathered together
and will bless the Lord of the righteous.

14How blessed are those who love you!
They will rejoice in your peace.
Blessed are all who grieved over all your afflictions,
for they will rejoice over you
when they see all your glory,
and they will be glad forever.
My soul rejoices forever.

15Bless God, the great King,

16for Jerusalem will be built with sapphire and emerald,
your walls with precious stone,
and your towers and battlements with pure gold.

17The streets of Jerusalem will be paved
with beryl and ruby and stone of Ophir.

18All her lanes will cry, 'Hallelujah!' and give praise, saying,
'Blessed is God, who has exalted you forever.'"

Notes

  • v2 "He scourges and He shows mercy; He brings down to Hades and brings up again" — the song of Hannah: The LORD kills and makes alive; He brings down to Sheol and raises up (1 Samuel 2:6). Hades is the Greek for Sheol. Tobit has lived it: You have scourged me, and You have had mercy on me (11:15).

  • v6 "Who knows whether He will accept you and show you mercy?" — eleēmosynē, the book's word, here of what God does: the charity Tobit gave is what he hopes God will give.

  • v10 "so that His tent may be built in you again" — skēnē, the tent of the wilderness, the name for the house that is to be rebuilt.

  • v11 "Many nations will come from far away… bearing gifts" — Isaiah's vision: Nations shall come to your light… they shall bring gold and frankincense (Isaiah 60:3, 6).

  • vv16–17 "built with sapphire and emerald… streets… paved" — Isaiah's promise to the afflicted city, I will lay your foundations with sapphires… your gates of carbuncles (Isaiah 54:11–12). Revelation's city is built of the same stones (Revelation 21:18–21).

  • v18 "All her lanes will cry, 'Hallelujah!'" — allēlouia, the Hebrew Praise the LORD, kept as a word in the Greek.

chapters.title: Tobit's Last Words
chapters.html:
Tobit 14

Tobit's Charge

1So Tobit finished giving thanks.

2He was fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight, and after eight years he saw again. He kept giving charity, and he went on fearing the Lord God and giving thanks to Him.

3When he had grown very old, he called his son and his son's sons, and said to him, "My child, take your sons. I have grown old, and I am about to depart from this life.

4Go to Media, my child, for I am convinced that what Jonah the prophet said about Nineveh, that it will be overthrown, will come true. In Media there will be peace for a time. Our brothers will be scattered over the earth from the good land, and Jerusalem will be desolate, and the house of God in it will be burned down and will be desolate for a time.

5But God will again have mercy on them and bring them back into the land, and they will rebuild the house, though not like the first one, until the times of the age are fulfilled. After this they will return from their captivity and rebuild Jerusalem in splendor, and the house of God will be built in it gloriously, as the prophets have said of it.

6All the nations will turn to fear the Lord God in truth, and will bury their idols.

7All the nations will bless the Lord. His people will give thanks to God, and the Lord will exalt His people. All who love the Lord God in truth and righteousness will rejoice, showing mercy to our brothers.

8And now, my child, leave Nineveh, for what Jonah the prophet said will surely happen.

9But you, keep the law and the commandments, and be merciful and righteous, so that it may go well with you.

10Bury me properly, and your mother with me, and do not stay any longer in Nineveh. My child, see what Adam did to Ahikar who brought him up, how he brought him out of the light into the darkness, and how he repaid him. Ahikar was saved, but the other received his repayment, and he went down into the darkness. Manasseh gave charity and was saved from the deadly trap that was set for him, but Adam fell into the trap and perished.

11So now, my children, see what charity does, and how righteousness delivers." As he said these things, his life left him on his bed. He was a hundred and fifty-eight years old, and Tobias buried him with honor.

Tobias in Ecbatana

12When Anna died, he buried her with his father. Then Tobias went away with his wife and his sons to Ecbatana, to Raguel his father-in-law.

13He grew old with honor, and he buried his parents-in-law with honor, and he inherited their property and that of his father Tobit.

14He died at the age of a hundred and seven in Ecbatana of Media.

15Before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus took captive. Before he died he rejoiced over Nineveh. Amen.

Notes

  • v2 "fifty-eight years old… after eight years" — so the shorter Greek, which makes him a hundred and fifty-eight at his death (v11). The longer Greek has sixty-two for his age when he went blind, and other numbers for his life.

  • vv4, 8 "what Jonah the prophet said about Nineveh" — Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown (Jonah 3:4). The longer Greek names Nahum, whose whole book is against Nineveh.

  • v5 "they will rebuild the house, though not like the first one" — what the old men wept over when the foundation was laid (Ezra 3:12), and what Haggai asked: Is it not as nothing in your eyes? (Haggai 2:3). Tobit sees beyond it to a house built gloriously.

  • v10 "see what Adam did to Ahikar… Manasseh gave charity and was saved" — the story of Ahikar, betrayed by the nephew he raised. The shorter Greek gives the nephew as Adam and calls Ahikar Manasseh in the last line; the longer Greek names the nephew Nadab. The point is the book's: charity saves, and treachery falls into its own trap.

  • v11 "see what charity does, and how righteousness delivers" — the book's last word on its own word (1:3; 4:10; 12:9).

  • v15 "he heard of the destruction of Nineveh… he rejoiced" — Tobias, who obeyed his father and left, lives to hear that Jonah's word came true.
